text: There were 6 birds sitting on a tree branch. 2 birds flew away into the sky. How many birds are still on the tree?
explanation: [ICSE Class 1 Syllabus] Subtract the birds that flew away: 6 - 2 = 4 birds.
hint: Take away the smaller number from the total.

text: Which shape has 4 straight equal sides and 4 corners?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 1 Syllabus] A square has 4 straight equal sides and 4 corners.
hint: Look at the number of sides and corners.

text: Which number comes immediately AFTER 5 when counting forward?
explanation: [CBSE Class 1 Syllabus] When counting forward: 5, then 6.
hint: Count one more forward.

text: What is the young baby of a hen called?
explanation: [ICSE Class 1 Syllabus] A young baby hen is known as a chick.
hint: Think of what a little baby hen is named.

text: Which sense organ in our body helps us hear sweet music, birds singing, and ringing bells?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 1 Syllabus] Our ears are the sense organs used to hear sweet music, birds singing, and ringing bells.
hint: Think of the body part you use for this sense.

text: Which of these is a LIVING thing that can grow, breathe, and drink water?
explanation: [CBSE Class 1 Syllabus] Living things like rabbits grow, breathe air, and need food and water.
hint: Choose the creature that is alive.

text: Which part of a green plant are green and make healthy food for the plant using sunlight?
explanation: [ICSE Class 1 Syllabus] Leaves of a plant are green and make healthy food for the plant using sunlight.
hint: Think of the plant part mentioned.

text: Which of these letters is an English VOWEL?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 1 Syllabus] The 5 English vowels are A, E, I, O, and U. "O" is a vowel.
hint: Remember the 5 special vowels: A, E, I, O, U.

text: Which word RHYMES with the word "PIN"?

hint: Listen to the ending sound of the word.

text: What is the exact OPPOSITE word of "UP"?
explanation: [ICSE Class 1 Syllabus] The opposite of up is down.
hint: Think of the opposite condition.

hint: It keeps raindrops off your head.

text: If you have 2 red apples and your mother gives you 1 more green apples, how many apples do you have in total?
explanation: [CBSE Class 1 Syllabus] Count all the apples together: 2 + 1 = 3 apples.
hint: Add the two numbers together.

text: There were 6 birds sitting on a tree branch. 2 birds flew away into the sky. How many birds are still on the tree?

hint: Take away the smaller number from the total.

hint: Count one more forward.

hint: Think of what a little baby hen is named.

text: When 114 is divided by 9, what is the quotient and the remainder?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 4 Syllabus] Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder: 114 = (9 × 12) + 6.

explanation: [CBSE Class 4 Syllabus] Perimeter of a rectangle = 2 × (Length + Width) = 2 × (22 + 7) = 58 m.
hint: Formula: Perimeter = 2 × (l + w).

text: Express the 4-digit number 9590 in its expanded notation form:
explanation: [ICSE Class 4 Syllabus] Expanded form displays place values: 9000 + 500 + 90 = 9590.

explanation: [IGCSE Class 4 Syllabus] When adding fractions with identical denominators, add the numerators: 7/9.

text: Convert 2 kilograms (kg) into grams (g):
explanation: [CBSE Class 4 Syllabus] 1 kilogram = 1,000 grams. Therefore, 2 kg = 2 × 1,000 = 2000 grams.
hint: Multiply kilograms by 1,000.

text: Which type of human teeth are 8 sharp, chisel-shaped front teeth used for biting and cutting food?
explanation: [ICSE Class 4 Syllabus] Incisors are 8 sharp, chisel-shaped front teeth used for biting and cutting food.
hint: Look at the shape and function of the teeth.

text: How is a camel specially adapted to survive long journeys across the sandy Thar Desert?
options: Webbed toes for swimming and thick fur for sub-zero blizzards
Gills for breathing underground and soft delicate paws
Sharp claws for climbing trees and wings for gliding
Wide padded feet that do not sink into loose sand, and fat stored in its hump
explanation: [IGCSE Class 4 Syllabus] Broad padded soles prevent sinking into desert sand, and stored fat in the hump provides energy.
hint: Think of the camel as the Ship of the Desert.

hint: Think of the specific phase of the water cycle.

hint: Line up the decimal points.

text: Calculate the volume of a solid geometric cube with edge length 8 cm:
explanation: [IGCSE Class 5 Syllabus] Volume of a cube = Side³ = 8 × 8 × 8 = 512 cm³.
hint: Formula: Volume = side × side × side.

text: In geometry, an angle that measures greater than 0° but strictly less than 90° is classified as what?

hint: Look at the angle degree measurement.

text: How many total bones make up the adult human skeletal framework?
explanation: [ICSE Class 5 Syllabus] Babies are born with approx. 300 bones, many of which fuse together to form 206 adult bones.
hint: It is between 200 and 210 bones.

text: A chronic nutritional deficiency of Vitamin A leads to which health disorder characterized by inability to see clearly in dim evening light?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 5 Syllabus] Deficiency of Vitamin A causes Night Blindness (inability to see clearly in dim evening light).
hint: Think of the disease caused by lack of Vitamin A.

text: Which gas makes up the largest constituent (approx. 78%) of Earth's atmospheric air mixture?
explanation: [CBSE Class 5 Syllabus] Earth's atmosphere consists of approximately 78% Nitrogen, 21% Oxygen, and 1% trace gases.
hint: It is an inert gas that makes up nearly four-fifths of air.

text: By which natural mechanism are the seeds of the Coconut plant primarily dispersed to distant habitats?

hint: Look at the structural adaptation of the seed.

hint: It is the central latitude line.

explanation: [IGCSE Class 6 Syllabus] Rotation takes 24 hours and causes different parts of Earth to alternately face and turn away from the Sun.
hint: Rotation causes day and night.
topicTag: Motions of the Earth (Rotation and Revolution)

text: What do geographers call the solid rocky outer crust layer of Earth comprising rocks, soil, and landforms?
explanation: [CBSE Class 6 Syllabus] The Lithosphere (from Greek lithos = stone) is the solid crust of the Earth.
hint: Lithos means rock or stone.

text: Which modal verb expresses strong moral obligation or necessity: "Citizens _____ obey traffic safety laws."
explanation: [ICSE Class 6 Syllabus] "Must" indicates a compulsory requirement or mandatory obligation.
hint: Choose the modal indicating mandatory duty.

text: In geometry, what is the term for: "Any line segment connecting two arbitrary points on a circle's circumference"?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 6 Syllabus] Chord is defined as any line segment connecting two arbitrary points on a circle's circumference.
hint: Recall parts of a circle.

text: Plants with thin, green, tender stems that grow small in height and have few branches are classified as:
explanation: [CBSE Class 6 Syllabus] Herbs are small plants with soft, non-woody green stems (e.g. mint, coriander, wheat).
hint: Think of mint or grass.

text: Identify the correct preposition of time: "Our annual school sports meet will commence _____ Monday morning."
explanation: [ICSE Class 6 Syllabus] We use "on" with specific days and dates (on Monday, on October 2nd).
hint: Use "on" before days of the week.

text: What were the sacred hymns of the Rigveda, composed in ancient Vedic Sanskrit, dedicated to?
options: Gods and natural forces like Agni, Indra, and Soma
explanation: [IGCSE Class 6 Syllabus] The Rigveda consists of 1,028 hymns (Suktas) in praise of deities like Indra (war god) and Agni (fire god).
hint: Vedic hymns praised natural deities.

text: What is the value of the Roman numeral LXXIV in Hindu-Arabic numbers?
explanation: [CBSE Class 6 Syllabus] L = 50, XX = 20, IV = 4. Total = 50 + 20 + 4 = 74.
hint: Break it into L (50) + XX (20) + IV (4).

text: Evaluate the integer arithmetic expression: (-15) + (-12) - (-2) = ?
hint: Remember that subtracting a negative number equals adding a positive.

text: According to divisibility tests, a large whole number is divisible by 3 if and only if:
options: the sum of all its digits is a multiple of 3
explanation: [IGCSE Class 6 Syllabus] Divisibility rule for 3: the sum of all its digits is a multiple of 3.
hint: Recall the standard test rule for 3.

text: What is the complete prime factorization of the composite integer 84?
explanation: [CBSE Class 6 Syllabus] Prime factorization breaks 84 entirely into prime bases: 2² × 3 × 7.
hint: Divide repeatedly by prime numbers: 2, 3, 5, 7...

text: Solve for the unknown variable x in the algebraic equation: x + 5 = 17
explanation: [ICSE Class 6 Syllabus] Transpose 5 to the other side: x = 17 - 5 = 12.
hint: Subtract 5 from both sides.

text: Express the ratio of 20 minutes to 1 hour(s) in its simplest reduced form:
explanation: [IGCSE Class 6 Syllabus] Convert hours to minutes first: 1 hr = 60 mins. Ratio = 20 : 60 = 1 : 3.
hint: Convert both quantities to the same unit (minutes) first.

text: When dilute iodine solution is dropped onto a boiled potato slice and turns blue-black, which nutrient is confirmed present?
explanation: [CBSE Class 6 Syllabus] Iodine reagent reacts specifically with amylose starch to produce a characteristic deep blue-black complex.
hint: Iodine test is the standard test for starch.

text: Which physical separation technique is defined by: "separating insoluble tea leaves from brewed liquid tea using a fine mesh strainer"?
explanation: [ICSE Class 6 Syllabus] Filtration is the process of separating insoluble tea leaves from brewed liquid tea using a fine mesh strainer.
hint: Recall methods of separation of substances.

text: Which type of movable skeletal joint found at the Neck joining the head allows our head to bend forward/backward and turn sideways?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 6 Syllabus] The pivot joint at the Neck joining the head allows our head to bend forward/backward and turn sideways.
hint: Think of how this joint moves.

text: What kind of optical image is formed on the translucent tracing screen of a simple Pinhole Camera?
explanation: [CBSE Class 6 Syllabus] Light travels in straight lines (rectilinear propagation), causing rays from top and bottom of an object to cross at the pinhole, forming an inverted real image.
hint: Pinhole cameras produce upside-down images.

text: Which of these materials is an ELECTRICAL CONDUCTOR that permits electric current to flow through a circuit?
options: Dry wooden stick and Plastic comb
explanation: [ICSE Class 6 Syllabus] Metals like copper and iron have free mobile electrons that conduct electric current.
hint: Metals conduct electricity.

text: Which ancient Bronze Age civilization in India was renowned for its sophisticated brick architecture, covered underground drainage, and the Great Bath at Mohenjo-daro?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 6 Syllabus] The Harappan civilization (c. 2500 BCE) featured remarkable grid-pattern town planning and hygiene systems.
hint: It flourished along the Indus river basin.

text: Following the immense destruction and bloodshed of which war did Mauryan Emperor Ashoka renounce violence and embrace Buddhism?
explanation: [CBSE Class 6 Syllabus] The carnage of the Kalinga War deeply moved Emperor Ashoka to adopt Dhamma (non-violence) and spread Buddhism.

explanation: [ICSE Class 6 Syllabus] Divisibility rule for 3: the sum of all its digits is a multiple of 3.
hint: Recall the standard test rule for 3.

text: What is the complete prime factorization of the composite integer 84?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 6 Syllabus] Prime factorization breaks 84 entirely into prime bases: 2² × 3 × 7.
hint: Divide repeatedly by prime numbers: 2, 3, 5, 7...

text: Solve for the unknown variable x in the algebraic equation: x + 5 = 17
explanation: [CBSE Class 6 Syllabus] Transpose 5 to the other side: x = 17 - 5 = 12.
hint: Subtract 5 from both sides.

text: Express the ratio of 45 minutes to 3 hour(s) in its simplest reduced form:
explanation: [ICSE Class 6 Syllabus] Convert hours to minutes first: 3 hr = 180 mins. Ratio = 45 : 180 = 1 : 4.
hint: Convert both quantities to the same unit (minutes) first.

text: When dilute iodine solution is dropped onto a boiled potato slice and turns blue-black, which nutrient is confirmed present?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 6 Syllabus] Iodine reagent reacts specifically with amylose starch to produce a characteristic deep blue-black complex.
hint: Iodine test is the standard test for starch.

text: Which physical separation technique is defined by: "separating lighter chaff and husk from heavier wheat grains using wind or blowing air"?
explanation: [CBSE Class 6 Syllabus] Winnowing is the process of separating lighter chaff and husk from heavier wheat grains using wind or blowing air.
hint: Recall methods of separation of substances.

text: Which type of movable skeletal joint found at the Elbows and Knees allows back-and-forth movement in one single plane like a door hinge?
explanation: [ICSE Class 6 Syllabus] The hinge joint at the Elbows and Knees allows back-and-forth movement in one single plane like a door hinge.
hint: Think of how this joint moves.

text: What kind of optical image is formed on the translucent tracing screen of a simple Pinhole Camera?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 6 Syllabus] Light travels in straight lines (rectilinear propagation), causing rays from top and bottom of an object to cross at the pinhole, forming an inverted real image.
hint: Pinhole cameras produce upside-down images.

text: Which of these materials is an ELECTRICAL CONDUCTOR that permits electric current to flow through a circuit?
options: Dry wooden stick and Plastic comb
explanation: [CBSE Class 6 Syllabus] Metals like copper and iron have free mobile electrons that conduct electric current.
hint: Metals conduct electricity.

text: Which ancient Bronze Age civilization in India was renowned for its sophisticated brick architecture, covered underground drainage, and the Great Bath at Mohenjo-daro?
explanation: [ICSE Class 6 Syllabus] The Harappan civilization (c. 2500 BCE) featured remarkable grid-pattern town planning and hygiene systems.
hint: It flourished along the Indus river basin.

text: Following the immense destruction and bloodshed of which war did Mauryan Emperor Ashoka renounce violence and embrace Buddhism?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 6 Syllabus] The carnage of the Kalinga War deeply moved Emperor Ashoka to adopt Dhamma (non-violence) and spread Buddhism.
hint: It was fought in modern-day Odisha.
topicTag: Emperor Ashoka and the Mauryan Empire

text: The Earth's daily rotation on its tilted axis from West to East causes which fundamental natural phenomenon?
options: The alternating cycle of Day and Night
explanation: [CBSE Class 6 Syllabus] Rotation takes 24 hours and causes different parts of Earth to alternately face and turn away from the Sun.
hint: Rotation causes day and night.
topicTag: Motions of the Earth (Rotation and Revolution)

text: What do geographers call the solid rocky outer crust layer of Earth comprising rocks, soil, and landforms?
explanation: [ICSE Class 6 Syllabus] The Lithosphere (from Greek lithos = stone) is the solid crust of the Earth.
hint: Lithos means rock or stone.

text: Which modal verb expresses strong moral obligation or necessity: "Citizens _____ obey traffic safety laws."
explanation: [IGCSE Class 6 Syllabus] "Must" indicates a compulsory requirement or mandatory obligation.
hint: Choose the modal indicating mandatory duty.

text: In geometry, what is the term for: "A line segment that passes straight through the center of a circle connecting two points on the circumference"?
explanation: [CBSE Class 6 Syllabus] Diameter is defined as a line segment that passes straight through the center of a circle connecting two points on the circumference.
hint: Recall parts of a circle.

text: Plants with thin, green, tender stems that grow small in height and have few branches are classified as:

hint: Think of mint or grass.

text: Identify the correct preposition of time: "Our annual school sports meet will commence _____ Monday morning."

hint: Use "on" before days of the week.

hint: Lithos means rock or stone.

text: Which modal verb expresses strong moral obligation or necessity: "Citizens _____ obey traffic safety laws."
explanation: [IGCSE Class 6 Syllabus] "Must" indicates a compulsory requirement or mandatory obligation.
hint: Choose the modal indicating mandatory duty.

text: In geometry, what is the term for: "A line segment that passes straight through the center of a circle connecting two points on the circumference"?
explanation: [CBSE Class 6 Syllabus] Diameter is defined as a line segment that passes straight through the center of a circle connecting two points on the circumference.
hint: Recall parts of a circle.

text: Plants with thin, green, tender stems that grow small in height and have few branches are classified as:
explanation: [ICSE Class 6 Syllabus] Herbs are small plants with soft, non-woody green stems (e.g. mint, coriander, wheat).
hint: Think of mint or grass.

text: Identify the correct preposition of time: "Our annual school sports meet will commence _____ Monday morning."
explanation: [IGCSE Class 6 Syllabus] We use "on" with specific days and dates (on Monday, on October 2nd).
hint: Use "on" before days of the week.

text: What were the sacred hymns of the Rigveda, composed in ancient Vedic Sanskrit, dedicated to?
options: Gods and natural forces like Agni, Indra, and Soma
explanation: [CBSE Class 6 Syllabus] The Rigveda consists of 1,028 hymns (Suktas) in praise of deities like Indra (war god) and Agni (fire god).
hint: Vedic hymns praised natural deities.

text: What is the value of the Roman numeral LXXIV in Hindu-Arabic numbers?
explanation: [ICSE Class 6 Syllabus] L = 50, XX = 20, IV = 4. Total = 50 + 20 + 4 = 74.
hint: Break it into L (50) + XX (20) + IV (4).

text: Evaluate the integer arithmetic expression: (-10) + (-16) - (-2) = ?
hint: Remember that subtracting a negative number equals adding a positive.

text: According to divisibility tests, a large whole number is divisible by 3 if and only if:
options: the sum of all its digits is a multiple of 3
explanation: [CBSE Class 6 Syllabus] Divisibility rule for 3: the sum of all its digits is a multiple of 3.
hint: Recall the standard test rule for 3.

text: What is the complete prime factorization of the composite integer 84?
explanation: [ICSE Class 6 Syllabus] Prime factorization breaks 84 entirely into prime bases: 2² × 3 × 7.
hint: Divide repeatedly by prime numbers: 2, 3, 5, 7...

text: Solve for the unknown variable x in the algebraic equation: x + 5 = 17
explanation: [IGCSE Class 6 Syllabus] Transpose 5 to the other side: x = 17 - 5 = 12.
hint: Subtract 5 from both sides.

text: Express the ratio of 30 minutes to 2 hour(s) in its simplest reduced form:
explanation: [CBSE Class 6 Syllabus] Convert hours to minutes first: 2 hr = 120 mins. Ratio = 30 : 120 = 1 : 4.
hint: Convert both quantities to the same unit (minutes) first.

text: When dilute iodine solution is dropped onto a boiled potato slice and turns blue-black, which nutrient is confirmed present?
explanation: [ICSE Class 6 Syllabus] Iodine reagent reacts specifically with amylose starch to produce a characteristic deep blue-black complex.
hint: Iodine test is the standard test for starch.

text: Which physical separation technique is defined by: "recovering common salt from seawater by heating liquid till water evaporates"?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 6 Syllabus] Evaporation is the process of recovering common salt from seawater by heating liquid till water evaporates.
hint: Recall methods of separation of substances.

text: Which type of movable skeletal joint found at the Shoulder and Hip joints allows complete 360° circular rotation in all directions?
explanation: [CBSE Class 6 Syllabus] The ball and socket joint at the Shoulder and Hip joints allows complete 360° circular rotation in all directions.
hint: Think of how this joint moves.

text: What kind of optical image is formed on the translucent tracing screen of a simple Pinhole Camera?
explanation: [ICSE Class 6 Syllabus] Light travels in straight lines (rectilinear propagation), causing rays from top and bottom of an object to cross at the pinhole, forming an inverted real image.
hint: Pinhole cameras produce upside-down images.

text: Which of these materials is an ELECTRICAL CONDUCTOR that permits electric current to flow through a circuit?
options: Dry wooden stick and Plastic comb
explanation: [IGCSE Class 6 Syllabus] Metals like copper and iron have free mobile electrons that conduct electric current.
hint: Metals conduct electricity.

text: Which ancient Bronze Age civilization in India was renowned for its sophisticated brick architecture, covered underground drainage, and the Great Bath at Mohenjo-daro?
explanation: [CBSE Class 6 Syllabus] The Harappan civilization (c. 2500 BCE) featured remarkable grid-pattern town planning and hygiene systems.
hint: It flourished along the Indus river basin.

text: Following the immense destruction and bloodshed of which war did Mauryan Emperor Ashoka renounce violence and embrace Buddhism?
explanation: [ICSE Class 6 Syllabus] The carnage of the Kalinga War deeply moved Emperor Ashoka to adopt Dhamma (non-violence) and spread Buddhism.
hint: It was fought in modern-day Odisha.
topicTag: Emperor Ashoka and the Mauryan Empire

explanation: [ICSE Class 6 Syllabus] The Rigveda consists of 1,028 hymns (Suktas) in praise of deities like Indra (war god) and Agni (fire god).
hint: Vedic hymns praised natural deities.

text: What is the value of the Roman numeral LXXIV in Hindu-Arabic numbers?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 6 Syllabus] L = 50, XX = 20, IV = 4. Total = 50 + 20 + 4 = 74.
hint: Break it into L (50) + XX (20) + IV (4).

text: Evaluate the integer arithmetic expression: (-5) + (-8) - (-2) = ?
hint: Remember that subtracting a negative number equals adding a positive.

text: According to divisibility tests, a large whole number is divisible by 3 if and only if:
options: the sum of all its digits is a multiple of 3
explanation: [ICSE Class 6 Syllabus] Divisibility rule for 3: the sum of all its digits is a multiple of 3.
hint: Recall the standard test rule for 3.

text: What is the complete prime factorization of the composite integer 84?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 6 Syllabus] Prime factorization breaks 84 entirely into prime bases: 2² × 3 × 7.
hint: Divide repeatedly by prime numbers: 2, 3, 5, 7...

text: Solve for the unknown variable x in the algebraic equation: x + 5 = 13
explanation: [CBSE Class 6 Syllabus] Transpose 5 to the other side: x = 13 - 5 = 8.
hint: Subtract 5 from both sides.

text: Express the ratio of 45 minutes to 3 hour(s) in its simplest reduced form:
explanation: [ICSE Class 6 Syllabus] Convert hours to minutes first: 3 hr = 180 mins. Ratio = 45 : 180 = 1 : 4.
hint: Convert both quantities to the same unit (minutes) first.

text: When dilute iodine solution is dropped onto a boiled potato slice and turns blue-black, which nutrient is confirmed present?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 6 Syllabus] Iodine reagent reacts specifically with amylose starch to produce a characteristic deep blue-black complex.
hint: Iodine test is the standard test for starch.

text: Which physical separation technique is defined by: "separating lighter chaff and husk from heavier wheat grains using wind or blowing air"?
explanation: [CBSE Class 6 Syllabus] Winnowing is the process of separating lighter chaff and husk from heavier wheat grains using wind or blowing air.
hint: Recall methods of separation of substances.

text: Which type of movable skeletal joint found at the Elbows and Knees allows back-and-forth movement in one single plane like a door hinge?
explanation: [ICSE Class 6 Syllabus] The hinge joint at the Elbows and Knees allows back-and-forth movement in one single plane like a door hinge.
hint: Think of how this joint moves.

text: What kind of optical image is formed on the translucent tracing screen of a simple Pinhole Camera?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 6 Syllabus] Light travels in straight lines (rectilinear propagation), causing rays from top and bottom of an object to cross at the pinhole, forming an inverted real image.
hint: Pinhole cameras produce upside-down images.

text: Which of these materials is an ELECTRICAL CONDUCTOR that permits electric current to flow through a circuit?
options: Dry wooden stick and Plastic comb
explanation: [CBSE Class 6 Syllabus] Metals like copper and iron have free mobile electrons that conduct electric current.
hint: Metals conduct electricity.

text: Which ancient Bronze Age civilization in India was renowned for its sophisticated brick architecture, covered underground drainage, and the Great Bath at Mohenjo-daro?
explanation: [ICSE Class 6 Syllabus] The Harappan civilization (c. 2500 BCE) featured remarkable grid-pattern town planning and hygiene systems.
hint: It flourished along the Indus river basin.

text: Following the immense destruction and bloodshed of which war did Mauryan Emperor Ashoka renounce violence and embrace Buddhism?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 6 Syllabus] The carnage of the Kalinga War deeply moved Emperor Ashoka to adopt Dhamma (non-violence) and spread Buddhism.
hint: It was fought in modern-day Odisha.
topicTag: Emperor Ashoka and the Mauryan Empire

explanation: [ICSE Class 7 Syllabus] 4x = 23 - 3 = 20 => x = 20 / 4 = 5.
hint: Subtract 3 from both sides and then divide by 4.

text: In a triangle ABC, interior angles measure ∠A = 42° and ∠B = 47°. What is the measure of angle ∠C?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 7 Syllabus] Angle sum property of a triangle: ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°. Therefore, ∠C = 180° - (42° + 47°) = 91°.
hint: The sum of angles in any triangle is 180 degrees.

text: A shopkeeper buys an article for ₹5000 and sells it for ₹6250. What is his profit percentage?
explanation: [CBSE Class 7 Syllabus] Profit = SP - CP = ₹1250. Profit % = (Profit / CP) × 100 = (1250 / 5000) × 100 = 25%.
hint: Formula: Profit% = (Profit / Cost Price) × 100.

text: Calculate the Simple Interest (SI) on a principal of ₹7000 at 6% per annum for 3 years:
explanation: [ICSE Class 7 Syllabus] Simple Interest = (P × R × T) / 100 = (7000 × 6 × 3) / 100 = ₹1260.
hint: Formula: SI = (P × R × T) / 100.

text: Find the area of a circle with radius r = 14 cm (Take π ≈ 22/7):
explanation: [IGCSE Class 7 Syllabus] Area of a circle = πr² = (22/7) × 14 × 14 = 616 cm².
hint: Formula: Area = π × r².

text: Which non-green parasitic plant lacks chlorophyll and winds its yellow tubular stems around host trees to absorb readymade food?
explanation: [CBSE Class 7 Syllabus] Cuscuta is a total stem parasite that derives nutrition directly from host vascular tissues.
hint: It is a yellow non-green twining climber.

text: Which organ of the human digestive system secretes BILE juice, stored in the gall bladder to emulsify fats?
explanation: [ICSE Class 7 Syllabus] The liver is the largest gland in the body and produces bile for digestion of fats.
hint: It is the largest internal reddish-brown gland.

text: Through which mode of heat transfer does thermal radiation from the Sun travel across millions of kilometers of empty vacuum to warm Earth?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 7 Syllabus] Radiation does not require any material medium; thermal waves travel through empty space at light speed.
hint: Conduction and convection both require material particles.

text: What products are formed during the chemical neutralization reaction between Hydrochloric Acid (HCl) and Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)?
explanation: [CBSE Class 7 Syllabus] Acid + Base -> Salt + Water + Heat: HCl + NaOH -> NaCl + H2O.
hint: Acid plus base yields salt and water.

text: During vigorous sprint running, temporary painful muscle cramps are caused by the accumulation of which compound due to anaerobic breakdown of glucose?
explanation: [ICSE Class 7 Syllabus] In lack of oxygen, muscle cells switch to anaerobic respiration: Glucose -> Lactic acid + energy.
hint: Anaerobic respiration in human muscle generates this organic acid.

text: Which complex plant vascular tissue is responsible for bidirectional transport of dissolved sucrose food synthesized by leaves to all other plant organs?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 7 Syllabus] Phloem transports organic food (translocation), while xylem transports water and minerals.
hint: Phloem conducts Food; Xylem conducts Water.

text: Who was the only woman monarch in history to ascend the throne of the Delhi Sultanate in 1236 CE?
explanation: [CBSE Class 7 Syllabus] Razia Sultana, daughter of Sultan Iltutmish, ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1236 to 1240 CE.
hint: She was nominated by Sultan Iltutmish.

text: Which great Mughal emperor established the policy of religious tolerance (Sulh-i-kul) and built the Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri?
explanation: [ICSE Class 7 Syllabus] Emperor Akbar promoted harmony among all religions and founded the ethical code Din-i-Ilahi.
hint: He was the third Mughal emperor.

text: Which major class of geological rocks is defined as: "formed when pre-existing rocks undergo extreme heat and pressure transforming into new minerals (e.g. Marble, Slate)"?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 7 Syllabus] Metamorphic Rocks are formed when pre-existing rocks undergo extreme heat and pressure transforming into new minerals (e.g. marble, slate).
hint: Recall the three primary rock families.

text: What crescent-shaped water body is formed when an undulating river meander loop gets cut off from the main river channel during floods?
explanation: [CBSE Class 7 Syllabus] River meander cut-offs form ox-bow lakes along flood plains.
hint: It looks like the crescent curved horn of an ox.

text: Convert to PASSIVE VOICE: "The skilled master chef baked a grand tiered cake for the celebration."
options: A grand tiered cake was baked by the skilled master chef for the celebration.
A grand tiered cake is baking by the skilled master chef.
The skilled master chef had been baked a grand tiered cake.
Baking a grand tiered cake by the skilled master chef.
explanation: [ICSE Class 7 Syllabus] Passive structure in simple past: Object + was/were + past participle (baked) + by + subject.
hint: The cake receives the action of being baked.

text: According to exponent laws, simplify the mathematical expression: 7^5 × 7^3
explanation: [IGCSE Class 7 Syllabus] Exponent product rule: a^m × a^n = a^(m+n). Therefore, 7^5 × 7^3 = 7^(5+3) = 7^8.
hint: Add the powers when multiplying powers with identical bases.

text: What is the physical time period of a simple oscillating pendulum that completes 20 full oscillations in 40 seconds?
explanation: [CBSE Class 7 Syllabus] Time Period = Total time / Number of oscillations = 40 s / 20 = 2.0 s.
hint: Divide time taken by the number of complete oscillations.

explanation: [ICSE Class 7 Syllabus] Personification attributes human actions (dancing) to non-human natural objects (leaves).

hint: An odd number of negative signs yields a negative product.

hint: It looks like the crescent curved horn of an ox.

text: Convert to PASSIVE VOICE: "The skilled master chef baked a grand tiered cake for the celebration."
options: A grand tiered cake is baking by the skilled master chef.
A grand tiered cake was baked by the skilled master chef for the celebration.
The skilled master chef had been baked a grand tiered cake.
Baking a grand tiered cake by the skilled master chef.
explanation: [CBSE Class 7 Syllabus] Passive structure in simple past: Object + was/were + past participle (baked) + by + subject.
hint: The cake receives the action of being baked.

text: According to exponent laws, simplify the mathematical expression: 7^5 × 7^3
explanation: [ICSE Class 7 Syllabus] Exponent product rule: a^m × a^n = a^(m+n). Therefore, 7^5 × 7^3 = 7^(5+3) = 7^8.
hint: Add the powers when multiplying powers with identical bases.

text: What is the physical time period of a simple oscillating pendulum that completes 20 full oscillations in 40 seconds?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 7 Syllabus] Time Period = Total time / Number of oscillations = 40 s / 20 = 2.0 s.
hint: Divide time taken by the number of complete oscillations.

text: Identify the figurative poetic device in: "The golden autumn leaves danced gracefully across the evening breeze."
explanation: [CBSE Class 7 Syllabus] Personification attributes human actions (dancing) to non-human natural objects (leaves).
hint: Human action attributed to inanimate objects.

text: Evaluate the product of three negative integers: (-3) × (-2) × (-3) = ?
explanation: [ICSE Class 7 Syllabus] Negative × Negative = Positive: (-3) × (-2) = +6. Then (+6) × (-3) = -18.
hint: An odd number of negative signs yields a negative product.

text: Solve for x in the linear equation: 4x + 3 = 39
explanation: [IGCSE Class 7 Syllabus] 4x = 39 - 3 = 36 => x = 36 / 4 = 9.
hint: Subtract 3 from both sides and then divide by 4.

text: In a triangle ABC, interior angles measure ∠A = 52° and ∠B = 57°. What is the measure of angle ∠C?
explanation: [CBSE Class 7 Syllabus] Angle sum property of a triangle: ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°. Therefore, ∠C = 180° - (52° + 57°) = 71°.
hint: The sum of angles in any triangle is 180 degrees.

text: A shopkeeper buys an article for ₹5000 and sells it for ₹6250. What is his profit percentage?
explanation: [ICSE Class 7 Syllabus] Profit = SP - CP = ₹1250. Profit % = (Profit / CP) × 100 = (1250 / 5000) × 100 = 25%.
hint: Formula: Profit% = (Profit / Cost Price) × 100.

text: Calculate the Simple Interest (SI) on a principal of ₹5000 at 6% per annum for 4 years:
explanation: [IGCSE Class 7 Syllabus] Simple Interest = (P × R × T) / 100 = (5000 × 6 × 4) / 100 = ₹1200.
hint: Formula: SI = (P × R × T) / 100.

text: Find the area of a circle with radius r = 14 cm (Take π ≈ 22/7):
explanation: [CBSE Class 7 Syllabus] Area of a circle = πr² = (22/7) × 14 × 14 = 616 cm².
hint: Formula: Area = π × r².

text: Which non-green parasitic plant lacks chlorophyll and winds its yellow tubular stems around host trees to absorb readymade food?
explanation: [ICSE Class 7 Syllabus] Cuscuta is a total stem parasite that derives nutrition directly from host vascular tissues.
hint: It is a yellow non-green twining climber.

text: Which organ of the human digestive system secretes BILE juice, stored in the gall bladder to emulsify fats?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 7 Syllabus] The liver is the largest gland in the body and produces bile for digestion of fats.
hint: It is the largest internal reddish-brown gland.

text: Through which mode of heat transfer does thermal radiation from the Sun travel across millions of kilometers of empty vacuum to warm Earth?
explanation: [CBSE Class 7 Syllabus] Radiation does not require any material medium; thermal waves travel through empty space at light speed.
hint: Conduction and convection both require material particles.

text: What products are formed during the chemical neutralization reaction between Hydrochloric Acid (HCl) and Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)?
explanation: [ICSE Class 7 Syllabus] Acid + Base -> Salt + Water + Heat: HCl + NaOH -> NaCl + H2O.
hint: Acid plus base yields salt and water.

text: During vigorous sprint running, temporary painful muscle cramps are caused by the accumulation of which compound due to anaerobic breakdown of glucose?

explanation: [CBSE Class 7 Syllabus] Phloem transports organic food (translocation), while xylem transports water and minerals.
hint: Phloem conducts Food; Xylem conducts Water.

text: Who was the only woman monarch in history to ascend the throne of the Delhi Sultanate in 1236 CE?

The skilled master chef had been baked a grand tiered cake.
A grand tiered cake was baked by the skilled master chef for the celebration.
Baking a grand tiered cake by the skilled master chef.
explanation: [ICSE Class 7 Syllabus] Passive structure in simple past: Object + was/were + past participle (baked) + by + subject.
hint: The cake receives the action of being baked.

text: According to exponent laws, simplify the mathematical expression: 7^5 × 7^3
explanation: [IGCSE Class 7 Syllabus] Exponent product rule: a^m × a^n = a^(m+n). Therefore, 7^5 × 7^3 = 7^(5+3) = 7^8.
hint: Add the powers when multiplying powers with identical bases.

text: What is the physical time period of a simple oscillating pendulum that completes 20 full oscillations in 40 seconds?
explanation: [CBSE Class 7 Syllabus] Time Period = Total time / Number of oscillations = 40 s / 20 = 2.0 s.
hint: Divide time taken by the number of complete oscillations.

text: Identify the figurative poetic device in: "The golden autumn leaves danced gracefully across the evening breeze."
explanation: [ICSE Class 7 Syllabus] Personification attributes human actions (dancing) to non-human natural objects (leaves).
hint: Human action attributed to inanimate objects.

text: Evaluate the product of three negative integers: (-3) × (-2) × (-4) = ?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 7 Syllabus] Negative × Negative = Positive: (-3) × (-2) = +6. Then (+6) × (-4) = -24.
hint: An odd number of negative signs yields a negative product.

text: Solve for x in the linear equation: 4x + 3 = 31
explanation: [CBSE Class 7 Syllabus] 4x = 31 - 3 = 28 => x = 28 / 4 = 7.
hint: Subtract 3 from both sides and then divide by 4.

text: In a triangle ABC, interior angles measure ∠A = 62° and ∠B = 67°. What is the measure of angle ∠C?
explanation: [ICSE Class 7 Syllabus] Angle sum property of a triangle: ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°. Therefore, ∠C = 180° - (62° + 67°) = 51°.
hint: The sum of angles in any triangle is 180 degrees.

text: A shopkeeper buys an article for ₹5000 and sells it for ₹6250. What is his profit percentage?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 7 Syllabus] Profit = SP - CP = ₹1250. Profit % = (Profit / CP) × 100 = (1250 / 5000) × 100 = 25%.
hint: Formula: Profit% = (Profit / Cost Price) × 100.

text: Calculate the Simple Interest (SI) on a principal of ₹3000 at 6% per annum for 2 years:
explanation: [CBSE Class 7 Syllabus] Simple Interest = (P × R × T) / 100 = (3000 × 6 × 2) / 100 = ₹360.
hint: Formula: SI = (P × R × T) / 100.

text: Find the area of a circle with radius r = 14 cm (Take π ≈ 22/7):
explanation: [ICSE Class 7 Syllabus] Area of a circle = πr² = (22/7) × 14 × 14 = 616 cm².
hint: Formula: Area = π × r².

text: Which non-green parasitic plant lacks chlorophyll and winds its yellow tubular stems around host trees to absorb readymade food?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 7 Syllabus] Cuscuta is a total stem parasite that derives nutrition directly from host vascular tissues.
hint: It is a yellow non-green twining climber.

text: Which organ of the human digestive system secretes BILE juice, stored in the gall bladder to emulsify fats?
explanation: [CBSE Class 7 Syllabus] The liver is the largest gland in the body and produces bile for digestion of fats.
hint: It is the largest internal reddish-brown gland.

text: Through which mode of heat transfer does thermal radiation from the Sun travel across millions of kilometers of empty vacuum to warm Earth?
explanation: [ICSE Class 7 Syllabus] Radiation does not require any material medium; thermal waves travel through empty space at light speed.
hint: Conduction and convection both require material particles.

text: What products are formed during the chemical neutralization reaction between Hydrochloric Acid (HCl) and Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 7 Syllabus] Acid + Base -> Salt + Water + Heat: HCl + NaOH -> NaCl + H2O.
hint: Acid plus base yields salt and water.

text: During vigorous sprint running, temporary painful muscle cramps are caused by the accumulation of which compound due to anaerobic breakdown of glucose?
explanation: [CBSE Class 7 Syllabus] In lack of oxygen, muscle cells switch to anaerobic respiration: Glucose -> Lactic acid + energy.
hint: Anaerobic respiration in human muscle generates this organic acid.

text: Which complex plant vascular tissue is responsible for bidirectional transport of dissolved sucrose food synthesized by leaves to all other plant organs?
explanation: [ICSE Class 7 Syllabus] Phloem transports organic food (translocation), while xylem transports water and minerals.
hint: Phloem conducts Food; Xylem conducts Water.

text: Who was the only woman monarch in history to ascend the throne of the Delhi Sultanate in 1236 CE?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 7 Syllabus] Razia Sultana, daughter of Sultan Iltutmish, ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1236 to 1240 CE.
hint: She was nominated by Sultan Iltutmish.

text: Which great Mughal emperor established the policy of religious tolerance (Sulh-i-kul) and built the Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri?
explanation: [CBSE Class 7 Syllabus] Emperor Akbar promoted harmony among all religions and founded the ethical code Din-i-Ilahi.
hint: He was the third Mughal emperor.

text: Which major class of geological rocks is defined as: "formed from layers of compressed, cemented mineral fragments and fossils over millions of years (e.g. Sandstone, Limestone)"?
explanation: [ICSE Class 7 Syllabus] Sedimentary Rocks are formed from layers of compressed, cemented mineral fragments and fossils over millions of years (e.g. sandstone, limestone).
hint: Recall the three primary rock families.

text: What crescent-shaped water body is formed when an undulating river meander loop gets cut off from the main river channel during floods?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 7 Syllabus] River meander cut-offs form ox-bow lakes along flood plains.
hint: It looks like the crescent curved horn of an ox.

explanation: [IGCSE Class 8 Syllabus] Since 26 × 26 = 676, √676 = 26.

hint: Formula: A = P(1 + r/100)^n.

hint: Formula: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b².

text: What is the mathematical formula for the volume of a right circular cylinder with radius r and height h?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 8 Syllabus] The volume of a cylinder equals base circular area multiplied by height: V = πr²h.
hint: Area of circle times height.

text: In Indian agriculture, which crop season is defined as: "sown in June-July at monsoon onset and harvested in September-October (e.g. Paddy rice, Maize, Cotton)"?
explanation: [CBSE Class 8 Syllabus] Kharif Crops are sown in june-july at monsoon onset and harvested in september-october (e.g. paddy rice, maize, cotton).
hint: Recall Indian seasonal crop cycles.

text: Which symbiotic soil bacterium dwells inside root nodules of leguminous pulses (dal) to convert atmospheric nitrogen into plant-absorbable nitrates?
explanation: [ICSE Class 8 Syllabus] Rhizobium fixes nitrogen symbiotically in leguminous root nodules, enriching soil fertility naturally.
hint: It fixes atmospheric nitrogen in pulse crops.

text: Which vital cellular organelle is designated as the "Powerhouse of the Cell" because it synthesizes cellular energy in the form of ATP molecules?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 8 Syllabus] Mitochondria perform aerobic cellular respiration, releasing energy stored in ATP molecules.
hint: It generates ATP for cell activities.

text: Why are circular steel ball bearings installed inside rotating mechanisms like bicycle wheels and electric ceiling fans?
options: To substitute high sliding friction with substantially lower rolling friction
explanation: [CBSE Class 8 Syllabus] Rolling friction is substantially smaller than sliding friction, drastically reducing heat and energy wastage.
hint: Rolling friction is much less than sliding friction.

text: What fundamental wave characteristic of acoustic vibrations governs the shrillness or pitch of a sound?
options: Frequency of vibration (measured in Hertz, Hz)
explanation: [ICSE Class 8 Syllabus] Pitch is determined by frequency (higher frequency = shriller pitch). Loudness is determined by amplitude.
hint: Higher frequency produces higher pitch.

text: Which industrial chemical process deposits a thin protective coating of a corrosion-resistant metal (like Chromium or Zinc) over another metal using electric current?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 8 Syllabus] Electroplating uses electrolysis to deposit a protective metal layer onto conductive cathodes.
hint: Coating metal via electric current.

text: In which historic battle in 1757 did Robert Clive's British East India Company forces defeat Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah, establishing colonial political dominion in Bengal?
explanation: [CBSE Class 8 Syllabus] The Battle of Plassey (June 23, 1757) marked the inception of British political rule in India.
hint: Fought in Bengal in 1757.

text: Which valiant warrior queen led the historic 1857 uprising against the British forces at Jhansi with the battle cry "Main apni Jhansi nahi doongi"?
explanation: [ICSE Class 8 Syllabus] Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi fought heroically against British commander Sir Hugh Rose during the 1857 Revolt.
hint: The warrior queen of Jhansi.

text: What is the apex and highest court of judicial appeal under the unified judicial hierarchy of the Republic of India?
options: The Supreme Court of India (New Delhi)
explanation: [IGCSE Class 8 Syllabus] The Supreme Court of India is the highest judicial constitutional court with final appellate jurisdiction.
hint: Headed by the Chief Justice of India.

explanation: [ICSE Class 8 Syllabus] Transpose terms: (4 - 3)x = -1 + 4 => 1x = 3 => x = 3.
hint: Group terms with x on one side and constants on the other.

text: In which quadrant of the two-dimensional Cartesian plane does the coordinate point P(-3, -4) lie?
explanation: [ICSE Class 9 Syllabus] Points with both negative coordinates (-x, -y) are located in Quadrant III.
hint: Both x and y are negative.

hint: Formula: Area = √(s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)).

text: According to circle theorems, if the angle subtended by an arc at the center of a circle is 86°, what is the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining circumference?
explanation: [CBSE Class 9 Syllabus] The angle subtended by an arc at the center is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle: 86° / 2 = 43°.
hint: The center angle is twice the circumference angle.

text: A sports car accelerates uniformly from rest at a = 2 m/s² for 4 seconds. What is its final velocity v?
explanation: [ICSE Class 9 Syllabus] Using first equation of motion: v = u + at = 0 + (2 × 4) = 8 m/s.
hint: Formula: v = u + at.

text: According to Newton's Second Law of Motion, what net force F is required to accelerate a vehicle of mass 3000 kg at 4 m/s²?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 9 Syllabus] Force = mass × acceleration = 3000 kg × 4 m/s² = 12000 Newtons (N).
hint: Formula: F = m × a.

text: According to Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation, if the distance r between two spherical planetary masses is DOUBLED, the mutual gravitational force F will:
explanation: [CBSE Class 9 Syllabus] Gravitational force obeys the inverse-square law: F ∝ 1/r². When r is doubled, F becomes 1/(2)² = 1/4 of the original force.
hint: Force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance.

text: Calculate the Kinetic Energy (Ek) of an object with mass m = 5 kg moving at a constant speed of v = 5 m/s:
explanation: [ICSE Class 9 Syllabus] Kinetic Energy formula: Ek = 1/2 m v² = 0.5 × 5 × (5)² = 62.5 J.
hint: Formula: Ek = 1/2 m v².

text: Which optical phenomenon describes the visible scattering of a beam of light by suspended colloidal particles in a mixture?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 9 Syllabus] The Tyndall effect is the scattering of light rays by colloidal particles, rendering the light path visible (e.g. sunlight through fog).
hint: Scattering of light by colloidal particles.

text: According to the mole concept, how many representative particles (atoms/molecules) are contained in exactly ONE mole of any substance?
explanation: [CBSE Class 9 Syllabus] One mole is defined as containing exactly 6.02214076 × 10²³ elementary entities (Avogadro's number NA).
hint: Avogadro's famous number.

text: Who performed the historic alpha-particle gold foil scattering experiment in 1911, demonstrating the discovery of the dense positively charged atomic nucleus?
explanation: [ICSE Class 9 Syllabus] Rutherford's alpha particle scattering experiment showed that most of the atom is empty space with a tiny, dense positive nucleus.
hint: Gold foil experiment scientist.

text: Which cellular digestive organelles are termed the "Suicide Bags of the Cell" because their powerful hydrolytic enzymes digest the cell itself during autolysis?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 9 Syllabus] Lysosomes contain membrane-bound hydrolytic digestive enzymes that break down cellular debris or autolyze dying cells.
hint: Cell organelle with digestive enzymes.
topicTag: Cell - The Fundamental Unit of Life

text: Which complex permanent vascular plant tissue conducts water and dissolved soil mineral nutrients unidirectionally upward from roots to the canopy leaves?
explanation: [CBSE Class 9 Syllabus] Xylem (tracheids and vessels) conducts water and minerals upward from roots, driven by transpirational pull.
hint: Conducts water upward from roots.

text: On July 14, 1789, angry citizens of Paris stormed and demolished which medieval royal fortress prison, igniting the French Revolution?
explanation: [ICSE Class 9 Syllabus] The storming of the Bastille on 14 July 1789 marked the dramatic opening insurrection of the French Revolution.
hint: Famous French fortress prison stormed in 1789.

text: Who led the Bolshevik faction of the Russian Social Democratic Labour Party that seized power during the Russian October Revolution of 1917?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 9 Syllabus] Vladimir Lenin led the Bolsheviks in overthrowing the Provisional Government in October 1917, founding Soviet Russia.
hint: Leader of the Bolshevik revolution.
topicTag: Socialism in Europe and the Russian Revolution

text: Which imaginary line of latitude passes almost midway through the central territory of India at 23°30' N latitude?
explanation: [CBSE Class 9 Syllabus] The Tropic of Cancer (23°30' N) passes through 8 Indian states, dividing the country into subtropical and tropical zones.
hint: 23.5 degrees North latitude line.

text: If the polynomial P(x) = x³ - 3x² + 4x - 12 has a zero at x = 3, what is the value of P(3)?
explanation: [ICSE Class 9 Syllabus] By definition of a zero of a polynomial: P(3) = 3³ - 3(3²) + 4(3) - 12 = 27 - 27 + 12 - 12 = 0.
hint: The value of a polynomial at its root is zero.

text: What is the human audible frequency sound range that can be detected by normal healthy human ears?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 9 Syllabus] Human hearing range spans frequencies from 20 Hz (infrasonic threshold) to 20,000 Hz (ultrasonic threshold).
hint: 20 Hz to 20 kHz.

text: Which peninsula geological river forms the second largest river basin in peninsular India and is often celebrated as the "Dakshin Ganga"?
explanation: [CBSE Class 9 Syllabus] The Godavari is the longest peninsular river (1,465 km) originating in Nasik, Maharashtra, known as the Dakshin Ganga.
hint: Longest river of Peninsular India.

text: Which specialized fluid connective tissue consists of red blood corpuscles (RBCs), white blood cells (WBCs), and platelets suspended in liquid plasma?
explanation: [ICSE Class 9 Syllabus] Blood is a fluid connective tissue that transports respiratory gases, nutrients, and hormones throughout the body.
hint: Circulating liquid connective tissue.

explanation: [IGCSE Class 9 Syllabus] Multiply numerator and denominator by conjugate (√5 + √4): (√5 + √4) / (5 - 4) = √5 + √4.
hint: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate.

hint: Formula: Ek = 1/2 m v².

text: Which optical phenomenon describes the visible scattering of a beam of light by suspended colloidal particles in a mixture?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 9 Syllabus] The Tyndall effect is the scattering of light rays by colloidal particles, rendering the light path visible (e.g. sunlight through fog).
hint: Scattering of light by colloidal particles.

text: According to the mole concept, how many representative particles (atoms/molecules) are contained in exactly ONE mole of any substance?
explanation: [CBSE Class 9 Syllabus] One mole is defined as containing exactly 6.02214076 × 10²³ elementary entities (Avogadro's number NA).
hint: Avogadro's famous number.

text: Who performed the historic alpha-particle gold foil scattering experiment in 1911, demonstrating the discovery of the dense positively charged atomic nucleus?
explanation: [ICSE Class 9 Syllabus] Rutherford's alpha particle scattering experiment showed that most of the atom is empty space with a tiny, dense positive nucleus.
hint: Gold foil experiment scientist.

text: Which cellular digestive organelles are termed the "Suicide Bags of the Cell" because their powerful hydrolytic enzymes digest the cell itself during autolysis?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 9 Syllabus] Lysosomes contain membrane-bound hydrolytic digestive enzymes that break down cellular debris or autolyze dying cells.
hint: Cell organelle with digestive enzymes.
topicTag: Cell - The Fundamental Unit of Life

text: Which complex permanent vascular plant tissue conducts water and dissolved soil mineral nutrients unidirectionally upward from roots to the canopy leaves?
explanation: [CBSE Class 9 Syllabus] Xylem (tracheids and vessels) conducts water and minerals upward from roots, driven by transpirational pull.
hint: Conducts water upward from roots.

text: On July 14, 1789, angry citizens of Paris stormed and demolished which medieval royal fortress prison, igniting the French Revolution?
explanation: [ICSE Class 9 Syllabus] The storming of the Bastille on 14 July 1789 marked the dramatic opening insurrection of the French Revolution.
hint: Famous French fortress prison stormed in 1789.

text: Who led the Bolshevik faction of the Russian Social Democratic Labour Party that seized power during the Russian October Revolution of 1917?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 9 Syllabus] Vladimir Lenin led the Bolsheviks in overthrowing the Provisional Government in October 1917, founding Soviet Russia.
hint: Leader of the Bolshevik revolution.
topicTag: Socialism in Europe and the Russian Revolution

text: Which imaginary line of latitude passes almost midway through the central territory of India at 23°30' N latitude?
explanation: [CBSE Class 9 Syllabus] The Tropic of Cancer (23°30' N) passes through 8 Indian states, dividing the country into subtropical and tropical zones.
hint: 23.5 degrees North latitude line.

text: If the polynomial P(x) = x³ - 3x² + 4x - 12 has a zero at x = 3, what is the value of P(3)?
explanation: [ICSE Class 9 Syllabus] By definition of a zero of a polynomial: P(3) = 3³ - 3(3²) + 4(3) - 12 = 27 - 27 + 12 - 12 = 0.
hint: The value of a polynomial at its root is zero.

text: What is the human audible frequency sound range that can be detected by normal healthy human ears?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 9 Syllabus] Human hearing range spans frequencies from 20 Hz (infrasonic threshold) to 20,000 Hz (ultrasonic threshold).
hint: 20 Hz to 20 kHz.

text: Which peninsula geological river forms the second largest river basin in peninsular India and is often celebrated as the "Dakshin Ganga"?
explanation: [CBSE Class 9 Syllabus] The Godavari is the longest peninsular river (1,465 km) originating in Nasik, Maharashtra, known as the Dakshin Ganga.
hint: Longest river of Peninsular India.

text: Which specialized fluid connective tissue consists of red blood corpuscles (RBCs), white blood cells (WBCs), and platelets suspended in liquid plasma?
explanation: [ICSE Class 9 Syllabus] Blood is a fluid connective tissue that transports respiratory gases, nutrients, and hormones throughout the body.
hint: Circulating liquid connective tissue.

text: Rationalize the denominator of the surd fraction: 1 / (√5 - √4)
explanation: [IGCSE Class 9 Syllabus] Multiply numerator and denominator by conjugate (√5 + √4): (√5 + √4) / (5 - 4) = √5 + √4.
hint: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate.

text: In which quadrant of the two-dimensional Cartesian plane does the coordinate point P(-3, -6) lie?
explanation: [CBSE Class 9 Syllabus] Points with both negative coordinates (-x, -y) are located in Quadrant III.
hint: Both x and y are negative.

text: Calculate the area of a scalene triangle with sides a = 6 cm, b = 8 cm, and c = 10 cm using Heron's formula:
hint: Formula: Area = √(s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)).

text: According to circle theorems, if the angle subtended by an arc at the center of a circle is 86°, what is the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining circumference?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 9 Syllabus] The angle subtended by an arc at the center is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle: 86° / 2 = 43°.
hint: The center angle is twice the circumference angle.

text: A sports car accelerates uniformly from rest at a = 2 m/s² for 4 seconds. What is its final velocity v?
explanation: [CBSE Class 9 Syllabus] Using first equation of motion: v = u + at = 0 + (2 × 4) = 8 m/s.
hint: Formula: v = u + at.

text: According to Newton's Second Law of Motion, what net force F is required to accelerate a vehicle of mass 2000 kg at 3 m/s²?
explanation: [ICSE Class 9 Syllabus] Force = mass × acceleration = 2000 kg × 3 m/s² = 6000 Newtons (N).
hint: Formula: F = m × a.

text: According to Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation, if the distance r between two spherical planetary masses is DOUBLED, the mutual gravitational force F will:
explanation: [IGCSE Class 9 Syllabus] Gravitational force obeys the inverse-square law: F ∝ 1/r². When r is doubled, F becomes 1/(2)² = 1/4 of the original force.
hint: Force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance.

explanation: [IGCSE Class 9 Syllabus] Human hearing range spans frequencies from 20 Hz (infrasonic threshold) to 20,000 Hz (ultrasonic threshold).
hint: 20 Hz to 20 kHz.

text: Which peninsula geological river forms the second largest river basin in peninsular India and is often celebrated as the "Dakshin Ganga"?
explanation: [CBSE Class 9 Syllabus] The Godavari is the longest peninsular river (1,465 km) originating in Nasik, Maharashtra, known as the Dakshin Ganga.
hint: Longest river of Peninsular India.

text: Which specialized fluid connective tissue consists of red blood corpuscles (RBCs), white blood cells (WBCs), and platelets suspended in liquid plasma?
explanation: [ICSE Class 9 Syllabus] Blood is a fluid connective tissue that transports respiratory gases, nutrients, and hormones throughout the body.
hint: Circulating liquid connective tissue.

text: Rationalize the denominator of the surd fraction: 1 / (√5 - √4)
explanation: [IGCSE Class 9 Syllabus] Multiply numerator and denominator by conjugate (√5 + √4): (√5 + √4) / (5 - 4) = √5 + √4.
hint: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate.

text: In which quadrant of the two-dimensional Cartesian plane does the coordinate point P(-3, -6) lie?
explanation: [CBSE Class 9 Syllabus] Points with both negative coordinates (-x, -y) are located in Quadrant III.
hint: Both x and y are negative.

text: Calculate the area of a scalene triangle with sides a = 6 cm, b = 8 cm, and c = 10 cm using Heron's formula:
hint: Formula: Area = √(s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)).

text: According to circle theorems, if the angle subtended by an arc at the center of a circle is 86°, what is the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining circumference?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 9 Syllabus] The angle subtended by an arc at the center is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle: 86° / 2 = 43°.
hint: The center angle is twice the circumference angle.

text: A sports car accelerates uniformly from rest at a = 2 m/s² for 4 seconds. What is its final velocity v?
explanation: [CBSE Class 9 Syllabus] Using first equation of motion: v = u + at = 0 + (2 × 4) = 8 m/s.
hint: Formula: v = u + at.

text: According to Newton's Second Law of Motion, what net force F is required to accelerate a vehicle of mass 2000 kg at 3 m/s²?
explanation: [ICSE Class 9 Syllabus] Force = mass × acceleration = 2000 kg × 3 m/s² = 6000 Newtons (N).
hint: Formula: F = m × a.

text: According to Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation, if the distance r between two spherical planetary masses is DOUBLED, the mutual gravitational force F will:
explanation: [IGCSE Class 9 Syllabus] Gravitational force obeys the inverse-square law: F ∝ 1/r². When r is doubled, F becomes 1/(2)² = 1/4 of the original force.
hint: Force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance.

text: Calculate the Kinetic Energy (Ek) of an object with mass m = 5 kg moving at a constant speed of v = 4 m/s:
explanation: [CBSE Class 9 Syllabus] Kinetic Energy formula: Ek = 1/2 m v² = 0.5 × 5 × (4)² = 40 J.
hint: Formula: Ek = 1/2 m v².

text: Which optical phenomenon describes the visible scattering of a beam of light by suspended colloidal particles in a mixture?
explanation: [ICSE Class 9 Syllabus] The Tyndall effect is the scattering of light rays by colloidal particles, rendering the light path visible (e.g. sunlight through fog).
hint: Scattering of light by colloidal particles.

text: According to the mole concept, how many representative particles (atoms/molecules) are contained in exactly ONE mole of any substance?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 9 Syllabus] One mole is defined as containing exactly 6.02214076 × 10²³ elementary entities (Avogadro's number NA).
hint: Avogadro's famous number.

text: Who performed the historic alpha-particle gold foil scattering experiment in 1911, demonstrating the discovery of the dense positively charged atomic nucleus?
explanation: [CBSE Class 9 Syllabus] Rutherford's alpha particle scattering experiment showed that most of the atom is empty space with a tiny, dense positive nucleus.
hint: Gold foil experiment scientist.

text: Which cellular digestive organelles are termed the "Suicide Bags of the Cell" because their powerful hydrolytic enzymes digest the cell itself during autolysis?
explanation: [ICSE Class 9 Syllabus] Lysosomes contain membrane-bound hydrolytic digestive enzymes that break down cellular debris or autolyze dying cells.
hint: Cell organelle with digestive enzymes.
topicTag: Cell - The Fundamental Unit of Life

text: Which complex permanent vascular plant tissue conducts water and dissolved soil mineral nutrients unidirectionally upward from roots to the canopy leaves?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 9 Syllabus] Xylem (tracheids and vessels) conducts water and minerals upward from roots, driven by transpirational pull.
hint: Conducts water upward from roots.

text: On July 14, 1789, angry citizens of Paris stormed and demolished which medieval royal fortress prison, igniting the French Revolution?
explanation: [CBSE Class 9 Syllabus] The storming of the Bastille on 14 July 1789 marked the dramatic opening insurrection of the French Revolution.
hint: Famous French fortress prison stormed in 1789.

text: Who led the Bolshevik faction of the Russian Social Democratic Labour Party that seized power during the Russian October Revolution of 1917?
explanation: [ICSE Class 9 Syllabus] Vladimir Lenin led the Bolsheviks in overthrowing the Provisional Government in October 1917, founding Soviet Russia.
hint: Leader of the Bolshevik revolution.
topicTag: Socialism in Europe and the Russian Revolution

text: Which imaginary line of latitude passes almost midway through the central territory of India at 23°30' N latitude?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 9 Syllabus] The Tropic of Cancer (23°30' N) passes through 8 Indian states, dividing the country into subtropical and tropical zones.
hint: 23.5 degrees North latitude line.

text: If the polynomial P(x) = x³ - 3x² + 4x - 12 has a zero at x = 3, what is the value of P(3)?
explanation: [CBSE Class 9 Syllabus] By definition of a zero of a polynomial: P(3) = 3³ - 3(3²) + 4(3) - 12 = 27 - 27 + 12 - 12 = 0.
hint: The value of a polynomial at its root is zero.

text: What is the human audible frequency sound range that can be detected by normal healthy human ears?
explanation: [ICSE Class 9 Syllabus] Human hearing range spans frequencies from 20 Hz (infrasonic threshold) to 20,000 Hz (ultrasonic threshold).
hint: 20 Hz to 20 kHz.

text: Which peninsula geological river forms the second largest river basin in peninsular India and is often celebrated as the "Dakshin Ganga"?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 9 Syllabus] The Godavari is the longest peninsular river (1,465 km) originating in Nasik, Maharashtra, known as the Dakshin Ganga.
hint: Longest river of Peninsular India.

text: Which specialized fluid connective tissue consists of red blood corpuscles (RBCs), white blood cells (WBCs), and platelets suspended in liquid plasma?
explanation: [CBSE Class 9 Syllabus] Blood is a fluid connective tissue that transports respiratory gases, nutrients, and hormones throughout the body.
hint: Circulating liquid connective tissue.

text: Rationalize the denominator of the surd fraction: 1 / (√4 - √3)
explanation: [ICSE Class 9 Syllabus] Multiply numerator and denominator by conjugate (√4 + √3): (√4 + √3) / (4 - 3) = √4 + √3.
hint: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate.

text: For the quadratic equation 3x² - 5x + 4 = 0, evaluate the discriminant D = b² - 4ac and determine the nature of its roots:
explanation: [ICSE Class 10 Syllabus] D = b² - 4ac = (-5)² - 4(3)(4) = 25 - 48 = -23. If D < 0, no real roots exist.
hint: Calculate D = b² - 4ac.

text: Find the 10th term (a₁₀) of the Arithmetic Progression (AP): 5, 10, 15, ...
explanation: [IGCSE Class 10 Syllabus] AP general formula: a_n = a + (n - 1)d = 5 + (10 - 1) × 5 = 5 + 45 = 50.
hint: Formula: an = a + (n - 1)d.

text: Find the distance between the coordinate points A(2, 3) and B(6, 6) in the Cartesian plane:
explanation: [CBSE Class 10 Syllabus] Distance formula = √((x₂ - x₁)² + (y₂ - y₁)²) = √((6 - 2)² + (6 - 3)²) = √(16 + 9) = √25 = 5 units.
hint: Formula: d = √((x2-x1)² + (y2-y1)²).

text: Evaluate the fundamental trigonometric identity: sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = ?
explanation: [ICSE Class 10 Syllabus] By Pythagorean trigonometric identity derived from a right-angled triangle: sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1.
hint: Universal trigonometry identity.

text: What geometric theorem is true regarding tangents drawn from an external point to a circle?
options: The lengths of the two tangents drawn from an external point are equal
The tangents pass through the circle's center
The sum of their lengths equals the diameter
explanation: [IGCSE Class 10 Syllabus] Theorem: The lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal (PA = PB).
hint: Tangents from an outside point are equal.

text: According to the mirror formula for spherical mirrors, which mathematical relationship connects focal length f, image distance v, and object distance u?
explanation: [CBSE Class 10 Syllabus] Mirror formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u. (For spherical lenses it is 1/f = 1/v - 1/u).
hint: Mirror formula has a positive plus sign.

text: Which visual defect of the human eye prevents a person from seeing distant objects clearly (Myopia), and which corrective lens is prescribed?
options: Far-sightedness (Hypermetropia), corrected using a Convex lens
Presbyopia, corrected using a Cylindrical lens
Near-sightedness (Myopia), corrected using a Concave (Diverging) lens
Astigmatism, corrected using a Bifocal prism
explanation: [ICSE Class 10 Syllabus] In myopia, light rays focus in front of the retina; a concave lens diverges incoming rays onto the retina.
hint: Concave lens corrects myopia (near-sightedness).
topicTag: Human Eye and Defects of Vision

text: According to Ohm's Law (V = IR), if an electric heating appliance draws a current of I = 5 A from a V = 220 V source, what is its electrical resistance R?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 10 Syllabus] Ohm's Law: R = V / I = 220 V / 5 A = 44 Ω.
hint: Formula: R = V / I.

text: In Fleming's Left-Hand Rule used for electric motors, what physical direction is represented by the FOREFINGER?
options: Direction of Force / Motion on the Conductor
Direction of the Magnetic Field (North to South)
explanation: [CBSE Class 10 Syllabus] In Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: Thumb = Motion/Force, Forefinger = Magnetic Field, Center finger = Current.
hint: Forefinger points along the magnetic Field.

text: In the redox reaction: CuO + H₂ -(heat)-> Cu + H₂O, which substance undergoes OXIDATION?
options: None, it is a neutral reaction
explanation: [ICSE Class 10 Syllabus] Hydrogen gains oxygen to form H2O, hence H2 is oxidized. CuO loses oxygen and is reduced to Cu.
hint: Oxidation is the gain of oxygen.

text: A laboratory chemical solution turns red litmus paper blue. What is its pH value most likely to be?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 10 Syllabus] Bases turn red litmus blue and have a pH greater than 7 on the pH scale.
hint: Bases have pH > 7.
topicTag: Acids, Bases and the pH Scale

text: What is the exact chemical name and formula of Plaster of Paris (P.O.P.), prepared by heating Gypsum at 373 K?
explanation: [CBSE Class 10 Syllabus] Gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) heated to 373 K loses water of crystallization to form Plaster of Paris: CaSO4·1/2 H2O.
hint: Hemihydrate means half molecule of water.
topicTag: Acids, Bases and Salts (Plaster of Paris)

text: What is the general molecular formula for the homologous series of ALKENES containing one carbon-carbon double bond?
explanation: [ICSE Class 10 Syllabus] Alkanes = CnH2n+2, Alkenes = CnH2n (e.g. Ethene C2H4), Alkynes = CnH2n-2.
hint: Formula: CnH2n.

text: Which digestive enzyme secreted in human saliva begins the breakdown of dietary starch into maltose sugars?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 10 Syllabus] Salivary amylase hydrolyzes complex starch polysaccharides into maltose disaccharides in the mouth.
hint: Enzyme in saliva that digests starch.

text: Which thick muscular chamber of the human heart pumps freshly oxygenated blood into the systemic aorta to supply the entire body?
explanation: [CBSE Class 10 Syllabus] The left ventricle has the thickest myocardium to generate high arterial pressure for systemic circulation via the aorta.
hint: Pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta.

text: In Gregor Mendel's monohybrid genetic cross of pure breeding Tall (TT) and Dwarf (tt) garden pea plants, what is the PHENOTYPIC ratio in the F₂ generation?
explanation: [ICSE Class 10 Syllabus] Monohybrid F2 generation produces 1 TT (tall), 2 Tt (tall), 1 tt (dwarf), yielding a 3:1 phenotypic ratio.
hint: Phenotypic ratio is 3 : 1.

text: Which region of the human hindbrain maintains motor muscular coordination, body equilibrium, and physical balance?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 10 Syllabus] The cerebellum coordinates voluntary muscular actions and controls body posture and equilibrium.
hint: Hindbrain region for posture and balance.

text: In which year did Mahatma Gandhi lead the historic 240-mile Salt March from Sabarmati Ashram to the coastal village of Dandi?
explanation: [CBSE Class 10 Syllabus] Mahatma Gandhi initiated the Civil Disobedience Movement with the historic Dandi Salt March from March 12 to April 6, 1930.
hint: Dandi Salt March occurred in 1930.

text: In probability theory, what is the theoretical probability of drawing an ACE from a standard well-shuffled deck of 52 playing cards?
explanation: [ICSE Class 10 Syllabus] A deck of 52 cards contains exactly 4 aces: P(Ace) = 4 / 52 = 1 / 13.
hint: There are 4 aces in 52 cards.

text: According to the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic in IGCSE Class 10, every composite number can be uniquely expressed as:
options: A product of prime factors, apart from the order in which prime factors occur
The sum of two irrational numbers
A ratio of two odd integers
explanation: [IGCSE Class 10 Syllabus] Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic: Every composite number can be factorized as a product of primes uniquely up to factor order.
hint: Recall prime factorization uniqueness theorem.

text: For the quadratic equation 2x² - 5x + 3 = 0, evaluate the discriminant D = b² - 4ac and determine the nature of its roots:
explanation: [CBSE Class 10 Syllabus] D = b² - 4ac = (-5)² - 4(2)(3) = 25 - 24 = 1. If D < 0, no real roots exist.
hint: Calculate D = b² - 4ac.

text: Find the 10th term (a₁₀) of the Arithmetic Progression (AP): 5, 10, 15, ...

text: Find the distance between the coordinate points A(2, 3) and B(6, 6) in the Cartesian plane:

text: Evaluate the fundamental trigonometric identity: sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = ?

hint: Universal trigonometry identity.

text: What geometric theorem is true regarding tangents drawn from an external point to a circle?

The tangents pass through the circle's center
The sum of their lengths equals the diameter

hint: Formula: an = a + (n - 1)d.

text: Find the distance between the coordinate points A(2, 3) and B(6, 6) in the Cartesian plane:
explanation: [IGCSE Class 10 Syllabus] Distance formula = √((x₂ - x₁)² + (y₂ - y₁)²) = √((6 - 2)² + (6 - 3)²) = √(16 + 9) = √25 = 5 units.
hint: Formula: d = √((x2-x1)² + (y2-y1)²).

text: Evaluate the fundamental trigonometric identity: sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = ?
explanation: [CBSE Class 10 Syllabus] By Pythagorean trigonometric identity derived from a right-angled triangle: sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1.
hint: Universal trigonometry identity.

text: What geometric theorem is true regarding tangents drawn from an external point to a circle?
options: The tangents pass through the circle's center
The lengths of the two tangents drawn from an external point are equal
The sum of their lengths equals the diameter
explanation: [ICSE Class 10 Syllabus] Theorem: The lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal (PA = PB).
hint: Tangents from an outside point are equal.

text: According to the mirror formula for spherical mirrors, which mathematical relationship connects focal length f, image distance v, and object distance u?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 10 Syllabus] Mirror formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u. (For spherical lenses it is 1/f = 1/v - 1/u).
hint: Mirror formula has a positive plus sign.

text: Which visual defect of the human eye prevents a person from seeing distant objects clearly (Myopia), and which corrective lens is prescribed?
options: Far-sightedness (Hypermetropia), corrected using a Convex lens
Presbyopia, corrected using a Cylindrical lens
Astigmatism, corrected using a Bifocal prism
Near-sightedness (Myopia), corrected using a Concave (Diverging) lens
explanation: [CBSE Class 10 Syllabus] In myopia, light rays focus in front of the retina; a concave lens diverges incoming rays onto the retina.
hint: Concave lens corrects myopia (near-sightedness).
topicTag: Human Eye and Defects of Vision

text: According to Ohm's Law (V = IR), if an electric heating appliance draws a current of I = 5 A from a V = 220 V source, what is its electrical resistance R?
explanation: [ICSE Class 10 Syllabus] Ohm's Law: R = V / I = 220 V / 5 A = 44 Ω.
hint: Formula: R = V / I.

text: In Fleming's Left-Hand Rule used for electric motors, what physical direction is represented by the FOREFINGER?
options: Direction of Force / Motion on the Conductor
Direction of the Magnetic Field (North to South)
explanation: [IGCSE Class 10 Syllabus] In Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: Thumb = Motion/Force, Forefinger = Magnetic Field, Center finger = Current.
hint: Forefinger points along the magnetic Field.

text: In the redox reaction: CuO + H₂ -(heat)-> Cu + H₂O, which substance undergoes OXIDATION?
options: None, it is a neutral reaction
explanation: [CBSE Class 10 Syllabus] Hydrogen gains oxygen to form H2O, hence H2 is oxidized. CuO loses oxygen and is reduced to Cu.
hint: Oxidation is the gain of oxygen.

text: A laboratory chemical solution turns red litmus paper blue. What is its pH value most likely to be?
explanation: [ICSE Class 10 Syllabus] Bases turn red litmus blue and have a pH greater than 7 on the pH scale.
hint: Bases have pH > 7.
topicTag: Acids, Bases and the pH Scale

text: What is the exact chemical name and formula of Plaster of Paris (P.O.P.), prepared by heating Gypsum at 373 K?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 10 Syllabus] Gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) heated to 373 K loses water of crystallization to form Plaster of Paris: CaSO4·1/2 H2O.
hint: Hemihydrate means half molecule of water.
topicTag: Acids, Bases and Salts (Plaster of Paris)

text: What is the general molecular formula for the homologous series of ALKENES containing one carbon-carbon double bond?
explanation: [CBSE Class 10 Syllabus] Alkanes = CnH2n+2, Alkenes = CnH2n (e.g. Ethene C2H4), Alkynes = CnH2n-2.
hint: Formula: CnH2n.

text: Which digestive enzyme secreted in human saliva begins the breakdown of dietary starch into maltose sugars?
explanation: [ICSE Class 10 Syllabus] Salivary amylase hydrolyzes complex starch polysaccharides into maltose disaccharides in the mouth.
hint: Enzyme in saliva that digests starch.

text: Which thick muscular chamber of the human heart pumps freshly oxygenated blood into the systemic aorta to supply the entire body?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 10 Syllabus] The left ventricle has the thickest myocardium to generate high arterial pressure for systemic circulation via the aorta.
hint: Pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta.

text: In Gregor Mendel's monohybrid genetic cross of pure breeding Tall (TT) and Dwarf (tt) garden pea plants, what is the PHENOTYPIC ratio in the F₂ generation?
explanation: [CBSE Class 10 Syllabus] Monohybrid F2 generation produces 1 TT (tall), 2 Tt (tall), 1 tt (dwarf), yielding a 3:1 phenotypic ratio.
hint: Phenotypic ratio is 3 : 1.

text: Which region of the human hindbrain maintains motor muscular coordination, body equilibrium, and physical balance?
explanation: [ICSE Class 10 Syllabus] The cerebellum coordinates voluntary muscular actions and controls body posture and equilibrium.
hint: Hindbrain region for posture and balance.

text: In which year did Mahatma Gandhi lead the historic 240-mile Salt March from Sabarmati Ashram to the coastal village of Dandi?
explanation: [IGCSE Class 10 Syllabus] Mahatma Gandhi initiated the Civil Disobedience Movement with the historic Dandi Salt March from March 12 to April 6, 1930.
hint: Dandi Salt March occurred in 1930.

text: In probability theory, what is the theoretical probability of drawing an ACE from a standard well-shuffled deck of 52 playing cards?
explanation: [CBSE Class 10 Syllabus] A deck of 52 cards contains exactly 4 aces: P(Ace) = 4 / 52 = 1 / 13.
hint: There are 4 aces in 52 cards.

text: According to the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic in ICSE Class 10, every composite number can be uniquely expressed as:
options: The sum of two irrational numbers
A ratio of two odd integers
A product of prime factors, apart from the order in which prime factors occur
explanation: [ICSE Class 10 Syllabus] Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic: Every composite number can be factorized as a product of primes uniquely up to factor order.
hint: Recall prime factorization uniqueness theorem.

text: For the quadratic equation 4x² - 5x + 5 = 0, evaluate the discriminant D = b² - 4ac and determine the nature of its roots:
explanation: [IGCSE Class 10 Syllabus] D = b² - 4ac = (-5)² - 4(4)(5) = 25 - 80 = -55. If D < 0, no real roots exist.
hint: Calculate D = b² - 4ac.

text: What geometric theorem is true regarding tangents drawn from an external point to a circle?

text: Find the 10th term (a₁₀) of the Arithmetic Progression (AP): 5, 10, 15, ...

hint: Universal trigonometry identity.

text: What geometric theorem is true regarding tangents drawn from an external point to a circle?

The lengths of the two tangents drawn from an external point are equal
The sum of their lengths equals the diameter
explanation: [CBSE Class 10 Syllabus] Theorem: The lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal (PA = PB).
hint: Tangents from an outside point are equal.
